### Reference depth must identify the intercept, not only the slope

[DEPTH_REFERENCE_ANCHOR_2026-11-09.md](<DEPTH_REFERENCE_ANCHOR_2026-11-09.md>)

> A deterministic counterexample shows that the current query-centred depth
> expectation can leave substantial regional effects when the whole query has a
> different depth from its reference. With known slopes, a fourfold depth shift
> leaves centred residuals of minus/plus log(2), even with one unchanged genotype.
> An added true RNA gain contrast0.243 becomes negative,−0.450, in that expectation
> comparison. This is not a measured package DNA call or a biological false-split rate.

### Estimated reference depth effects: benefit depends on support and transport

[DEPTH_REFERENCE_ESTIMATION_2026-11-09.md](<DEPTH_REFERENCE_ESTIMATION_2026-11-09.md>)

> The conditional intercept correction reduces RNA-profile error with well-supported
> reference depth variation, but is unsafe as a universal correction. Estimated
> slopes amplify noise under narrow support and introduce effects when the true
> slopes are zero. Even known slopes cannot transport a reference-specific
> expression programme to a query lacking that programme. No production correction
> or calibration claim is promoted. Frozen evidence and criteria are unchanged.

### Label-invariant numerical audit preserves the failed clone tradeoff

[RNA_POPULATION_OPTIMIZER_2026-11-09.md](<RNA_POPULATION_OPTIMIZER_2026-11-09.md>)

> Correct the comparator's refinement diagnostic:67 cases had changed literal
> component labels, but4 were complete reversals of two arbitrary names. There
> are63 changed partitions among998 cases, with up to289 changed cells. None of
> the32 accepted evaluation distinctions changes partition under refinement.
> Independent optimization finds no material supported gain over the saved fine

> method correction is justified by this investigation.

### Count-splitting redraw stability: separate a law change from one realized split

[SPLIT_DRAW_STABILITY_2026-11-09.md](<SPLIT_DRAW_STABILITY_2026-11-09.md>)

> This is a development diagnostic on the five existing raw-count matrices.
> The known-gene-size research path changes both the splitting law and the realized
> count halves. Its canonical recovery improvement therefore does not, by itself,
> identify the law as the causal improvement. The experiment asks whether recovery
> persists under other count-splitting draws with all other random settings fixed.
> It does not select a best seed or create a new clinical error-control panel.

### A continuous-state alternative limits clone detection even before count noise

[STATE_INFORMATION_2026-11-08.md](<STATE_INFORMATION_2026-11-08.md>)

> Under one explicitly specified competing RNA-state model, the best possible
> level-5% specimen test has detection power at most0.1118242, with at least95%
> Monte Carlo confidence conditional on the stated laws and checked numerical
> enclosures. This is a600-cell oracle calculation, not a universal biological
> limit, a HaploDose performance estimate, or proof that the three original
> thinning assertions are impossible. Those failures and criteria remain intact.

### A predictive state safeguard fails recovery, so reject it

[STATE_PREDICTIVE_CONFIRMATION_2026-11-10.md](<STATE_PREDICTIVE_CONFIRMATION_2026-11-10.md>)

> The implemented discovery-to-confirmation predictive comparison does not solve
> the clone false-split/power tradeoff. It retains original case20261107 but rejects
> original case20261109; three of four known false splits favor continuous state,
> and the fourth is numerically unresolved. The prespecified six-case screen
> fails. Reject expansion and do not tune its threshold, override the original
> recovery assertion or claim5% error control. Production and frozen results are
> unchanged. All eight CPU jobs complete0:0.

### Discovery/confirmation allocation does not repair remaining recovery

[THINNING_ALLOCATION_2026-11-08.md](<THINNING_ALLOCATION_2026-11-08.md>)

> The objective is to retain independently supported CNA distinctions without
> weakening confirmation or increasing unsupported subdivisions. This locked
> development screen tests whether reallocating counts improves fitted membership
> information. Neither unequal allocation warrants promotion.

## Primary measurements, DNA truth and prospective feasibility

### One locked Kinker line retains donor-specific counts and phase

> historical mechanism investigation, not an estimate of population performance.

### Stable allele roles precede public raw-input discovery

[ALLELE_RAW_ROLES_2026-11-08.md](<ALLELE_RAW_ROLES_2026-11-08.md>)

> A research front end now partitions whole SNP sites before the unmodified public
> reader and complete raw-input pipeline. Eight public runs preserve identical
> scientific outputs within each of the two existing cell models when only reserved
> observations change. An independent audit verifies site roles, all row/count
> conservation and actual emitted tables/posteriors. This establishes tested
> computational isolation, not independent confirmation or clone accuracy.

### Andor DNA fetchers misplaced reads at exact bin boundaries

[ANDOR_DNA_COORDINATES_2026-11-08.md](<ANDOR_DNA_COORDINATES_2026-11-08.md>)

> Both Andor DNA fetchers now convert one-based SAM alignment starts to zero-based
> 500 kb bins with `floor((POS-1)/500000)`. Previously they used `floor(POS/500000)`,
> placing a start exactly divisible by 500000 in the following bin. The independent
> audit confirms ten such filtered reads in prespecified bounded archive queries.
> Historical counts, DNA labels and RNA scores remain unchanged. The effect on
> genome-wide DNA profiles or clone reconstruction is not established here.

> CPU/GPU simulation test passes,1 executed and0 skipped. Both backend assertions
> inside inference pass, together with existing malignant-call agreement>0.99,
> clone ARI>0.95, profile join>0.95 and correlation>0.999 criteria. Process peak
> RSS1627856KiB, scheduler peak1702020KiB;5s sampling observes owned GPU memory up

> wheel/native identities and actual GPU are recorded under analysis_23024875;

### Kinker measurement chain and complete-population scoring

[KINKER_MEASUREMENT_CHAIN_2026-11-09.md](<KINKER_MEASUREMENT_CHAIN_2026-11-09.md>)

### OneK1K: possible donor replication, unresolved CNA truth

[ONEK1K_FEASIBILITY_2026-11-08.md](<ONEK1K_FEASIBILITY_2026-11-08.md>)

> OneK1K is a potentially useful biological-control resource, not an accepted
> single-CNA null panel. The archive describes 982 healthy RNA donors and blood
> DNA genotyped with Illumina Global Screening Array-24 v2.0, including 18
> replicates. GSE196830 links RNA series GSE196735 and DNA series GSE196829. The
> DNA record lists a raw archive and a processed genotype matrix. Neither was
> downloaded. Array rows, repeated assays and pooled RNA libraries must not be
> counted as independent donors.
> [DNA series](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE196829),
> [RNA series](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE196735).

> The goal is independent validation of RNA-derived profiles and cell memberships,

### Prospective truth construction: source review

[PROSPECTIVE_SOURCE_REVIEW_2026-11-08.md](<PROSPECTIVE_SOURCE_REVIEW_2026-11-08.md>)

> This review narrows the outstanding measurement requirements for the two existing

> protocol text and source code were inspected; no per-cell measurements, clone

> Current repository and inspected blob identities are recorded in

> All98 legacy HCT116 GEO records have unique titles001-098 and unique description

### Published DNA has variable intervals and limited chromosome support

[SCONE_DNA_COORDINATES_2026-11-09.md](<SCONE_DNA_COORDINATES_2026-11-09.md>)

> The scONE cell-line normalized DNA table contains 5,393 variable-length intervals,
> with no interval exactly 500 kb. Its coordinate representation is consistent
> with one-based closed intervals. All autosomes reach their audited GRCh38 FAI
> ends, but the X block stops at 114,820,832; Y and mitochondrial DNA are absent.
> These are properties of published-table support, not observed neutral DNA or a
> validated biological deletion.

> single-CNA controls. The abstract and published biological descriptions were

## Uncertainty, confidence and information limits

### Joint reference, calibration and patient uncertainty for bulk amplitudes

[BULK_AMPLITUDE_UNCERTAINTY_2026-11-09.md](<BULK_AMPLITUDE_UNCERTAINTY_2026-11-09.md>)

> The [reference-sensitivity study](BULK_AMPLITUDE_REFERENCE_2026-11-09.md) found
> that several fixed-reference gains reversed when the normal reference changed.
> This stage estimates uncertainty without choosing a favourable reference,
> candidate, comparator or endpoint. It retains both continuous-amplitude
> estimators, all ten historical controls and all four endpoints: 80 contrasts.
> The [design](../dev/bulk_amplitude_uncertainty_20261109/DESIGN.md) was frozen
> before the pilot and before any uncertainty outcome was viewed.

### Fitted RNA membership confidence does not repair genomic membership

[CLONE_MEMBERSHIP_CONFIDENCE_2026-11-09.md](<CLONE_MEMBERSHIP_CONFIDENCE_2026-11-09.md>)

> [Observed pattern, not a guarantee] On all 1200 saved evaluation fits, high
> plug-in RNA coassignment confidence remains compatible with substantial genomic
> error. For the full-membership arm, mean per-specimen error among pairs assigned
> at least95% confidence is38.94% under the one-population state null and42.60%
> under the two-clone condition. A95% confidence cutoff therefore lacks support
> as the proposed membership correction. This does not establish that every
> possible abstention procedure fails.

### Dependence-aware protection of selected RNA intervals

[DEPENDENT_UNCERTAINTY_2026-11-08.md](<DEPENDENT_UNCERTAINTY_2026-11-08.md>)

> The objective is to narrow systematic-RNA intervals without weakening coverage
> after adaptive interval selection. The new research calculation accounts for
> overlap and covariance among all eligible intervals. It improves some simulated
> power measurements, but does not resolve the missing biological covariance and
> reference information. Production inference and uncertainty defaults are unchanged.

### Numerical uncertainty in the existing profile bootstrap

[PROFILE_MC_PRECISION_2026-11-08.md](<PROFILE_MC_PRECISION_2026-11-08.md>)

> Update: the fixed one-million-draw refinement and independent audit now resolve
> the correlation calculations' numerical precision. The original20000-draw
> finding below remains as history. No biological/reference limitation is removed.

### Why conservative RNA-effect intervals have low power

[UNCERTAINTY_ATTRIBUTION_2026-11-08.md](<UNCERTAINTY_ATTRIBUTION_2026-11-08.md>)

> The goal is useful uncertainty for the systematic regional RNA effect, while
> retaining coverage after interval selection. This analysis separates counting
> noise, latent/reference variation and the simultaneous penalty. It creates no
> new interval method, cutoff or biological validation claim.
